title: The Secret Yearbook
premise: Jude Sandoval has spent three years perfecting the art of being fine—cooking dinners, signing permission slips, and keeping their own wants folded small enough to fit between shifts. When best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her car keys and a half-finished secret yearbook project, Jude is forced into a search that unravels every careful arrangement of their life, including the truth that Priya was documenting the town's quiet cruelties—and Jude's complicity in them. As the final football game approaches, Jude must choose between protecting the family myth they've built and telling the truth that might finally let them belong. The story ends with Priya found alive but changed, the yearbook published against the school's wishes, and Jude stepping onto the field at halftime—not to play, but to be seen for the first time.
about_author: Paloma Lockridge grew up in a rust-belt town where Friday nights meant stadium lights and everyone knew which houses to look away from. She writes stories about kids who hold families together and the cost of never being held themselves.

chapters.title: Fine
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A Tuesday in October: school, grocery run, microwaved dinners, checking Marisol's homework while Mom's night-shift bus idles outside. Jude insists everything is fine so many times it becomes a spell. Emotional beat: the exhausting competence of a kid who has stopped expecting rescue.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Priya misses their standing Thursday milkshake, then doesn't answer texts. On Jude's porch: Priya's car keys, a sticky note reading 'finish it,' and nothing else. Police call it a runaway. Jude knows better. Beat: dread arriving quietly, like weather.

chapters.title: What Runaways Leave Behind
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude searches Priya's locker with a borrowed janitor key and finds a manila envelope: photos, clippings, and a mock-up titled 'The Secret Yearbook'—an unauthorized record of who this town really is. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Priya's journal entries interleaved. Flashback texture: how Priya and Jude became friends over shared invisibility—one the scholarship kid, one the caretaker. Priya's entries grow sharper, angrier about the school's quiet erasures. Beat: love with an edge of guilt.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The middle sibling has been keeping her own secrets—a failing grade, a friend she's hiding—and recognizes the shape of Jude's lies. She offers to help find Priya if Jude stops lying to her. Beat: siblings as reluctant allies.

chapters.title: Coach Delgado's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Coach offers Jude a spot on the team—full ride potential, a way out—if they keep their head down until season's end. It's everything Jude never let themselves want. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Pages
chapters.summary: Jude and Marisol's POV, alternating scenes. Decoding Priya's project: pages exposing hazing cover-ups, a teacher's misconduct ignored, booster-club money gone missing. One page has Jude's name in the margin: 'knew, said nothing.' Beat: shame made physical.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Exhausted, frightened by the missing-kid flyers, she confronts Jude about carrying too much for too long. Jude deflects; Mom sees through it but lets it go—for now. Beat: two people loving each other in the language of avoidance.

chapters.title: Someone Was Watching
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following Priya's last documented route, Jude notices a truck that keeps appearing. A threatening note appears in their own locker: STOP ASKING. Beat: the search turns dangerous; fear gets a body.

chapters.title: Theo
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Priya's older brother returns from college, furious and grieving, convinced Jude knows more than they're saying. Their friction sparks into uneasy partnership—and something warmer neither names. Beat: grief as a meeting place.

chapters.title: The Booster Club Dinner
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Undercover at the boosters' fundraiser, Jude overhears Principal Voss and a donor discussing 'the Priya problem' and a payment trail. They get photographic proof—at the cost of nearly blowing their cover. Beat: courage with shaking hands.

chapters.title: Half-Truths
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts Jude about the margin note—what did Jude know? Jude admits they saw the hazing photo months ago and stayed silent to protect their scholarship chances. Theo walks out. Beat: loyalty and truth tearing the same wound.

chapters.title: Marisol Runs
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Scared by the escalating threats, Marisol runs to Priya's old treehouse and finds fresh evidence someone's been living there—blankets, energy wrappers, Priya's handwriting. Beat: hope arriving disguised as a mess.

chapters.title: The Game They Made Me Play
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Forced onto the field to keep the coach's goodwill, Jude plays badly, distracted, then realizes the crowd includes the man from the truck. Afterward, their house has been searched. Beat: nowhere left that is safe or small.

chapters.title: What Priya Found
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (journal). Entries reveal why she ran: she'd traced the missing booster money to Voss, who threatened her family's immigration status. She didn't run away—she went underground to finish the yearbook safely. Beat: reframing everything; the missing girl chose disappearance.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using the treehouse clue, Jude leaves a message only Priya would trust: a page of the yearbook finished in their own hand. At 2 a.m., a text: 'you finished it?' Beat: relief and terror holding hands.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss suspends Jude pending 'welfare concerns,' confiscates the yearbook materials, and pressures Mom with veiled threats about her job. The adults close ranks. Beat: institutions showing their teeth.

chapters.title: The Treehouse Pact
chapters.summary: Jude, Marisol, and Theo's POV braided. The three meet Priya at dawn. She's scared, stubborn, alive. They plan to publish the yearbook digitally during the championship game, when the whole town will be watching one place. Beat: a found family choosing each other.

chapters.title: Friday Night Lights Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Halftime. As the stadium lights blaze, the yearbook uploads to every phone in the stands via the school's own Wi-Fi password—Priya's birthday. The crowd goes silent, then ugly, then loud. Beat: truth detonating in public.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Voss resigns under investigation; the donor is exposed; Coach, unexpectedly, defends Jude publicly. Priya comes home to her family. But Jude faces suspension and Mom faces hard questions about what she missed. Beat: victory that still costs.

chapters.title: When the Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Suspension hearing: Jude speaks—not as the responsible one, not as the scholarship kid, just as themselves, owning both silence and courage. The board relents. Mom takes a day shift; Marisol's grades get help; Theo holds Jude's hand in the hallway. Beat: belonging earned by honesty, not usefulness.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Spring. The printed Secret Yearbook arrives—unauthorized, beloved, passed hand to hand. Its final page is blank except for one line in Priya's writing: 'For everyone who was fine.' Jude signs their full name beneath it. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
